note: P4356 (Pro 29:24) — the partner of a thief hates his own life; he hears the curse but discloses nothing.

dims.v: self-destruction — complicity in theft that is self-hatred
the hating of one's own life shown by partnering with a thief — the complicity in crime that is, in effect, self-destruction, ruining the accomplice along with the thief
welded to the sworn silence that shares the guilt
sane (hate) — 'the partner of a thief HATES his own life'; to join in another's crime is to destroy oneself. The accomplice, in effect, hates his own life, courting the ruin his complicity invites.
guilty complicity — hearing the adjuration to testify, yet disclosing nothing
the hearing of the public curse/adjuration to testify while disclosing nothing — the guilty silence that, sworn to speak, withholds the truth and so shares fully in the crime
welded to the self-hatred complicity amounts to

shama (hear) — 'he HEARS the curse, but discloses nothing'; the accomplice, adjured under oath to testify, keeps guilty silence. To hear the truth demanded and withhold it is to share the guilt (cf Lev 5:1).
